title_english: Book of Jasher (Jashar)
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Poetic material: the sun and moon standing still (Josh 10:13) and David's lament 'the Bow' over Saul and Jonathan (2 Sam 1:18)
surviving_status: extant work with the same name but probably different
note: Usually understood as a collection of poems or war songs. A Hebrew midrash called Sefer haYashar (earliest surviving printing Venice, 1625; English translation by Moses Samuel, 1840) is not accepted in rabbinic Judaism as the biblical book. A different English 'Book of Jasher' printed by Jacob Ilive in 1751 is regarded as a forgery (per Wikipedia, checked Oct 2026).

title_english: Book of the Wars of the LORD
what_the_text_says_it_contains: A poetic fragment about Waheb in Suphah and the wadis of the Arnon
note: Only this one fragment is quoted; the Hebrew is obscure and translations differ widely.

title_english: Book of the Acts of Solomon
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The rest of Solomon's acts, all he did, and his wisdom

title_english: Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Further events of the reigns of northern kings (first cited for Jeroboam: how he warred and reigned)
note: Cited repeatedly through 1-2 Kings; only the first occurrence is listed here. Not the canonical books of Chronicles, which were written later.

title_english: Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Further events of the reigns of Judah's kings (first cited for Rehoboam)
note: Cited repeatedly through 1-2 Kings; only the first occurrence is listed here. Not the canonical books of Chronicles.

title_english: Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel / of Israel and Judah
title_hebrew_or_greek: סֵפֶר הַמְּלָכִים לִיהוּדָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל; סֵפֶר מַלְכֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Acts of Asa, Jotham and Hezekiah
note: Cited by Chronicles. Many scholars think this means the canonical books of Kings (or a source shared with them); others think it was a separate, fuller history.

title_english: Story (Midrash) of the Book of the Kings
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Joash's sons, the oracles against him, and the repair of the house of God
note: May be a commentary on, or the same as, the 'book of the kings' above.

title_english: Book of Samuel the Seer
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The acts of King David, first and last
note: Often equated with material in the canonical books of Samuel; debated.

title_english: Book of Nathan the Prophet
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Acts of David and of Solomon
note: Some scholars take the prophetic 'books' in Chronicles as sections of Samuel-Kings associated with each prophet.

title_english: Book of Gad the Seer
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The acts of King David
note: Same caveat as Nathan.

title_english: Prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Events of Solomon's reign
note: Ahijah's oracle to Jeroboam is narrated in 1 Kings 11:29-39.

title_english: Visions of Iddo the Seer
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Visions concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat; events of Solomon's reign
note: Hebrew spelling of the name varies here (Jedo / Iddo).

title_english: Book of Shemaiah the Prophet and of Iddo the Seer concerning genealogies
title_hebrew_or_greek: דִּבְרֵי שְׁמַעְיָה הַנָּבִיא וְעִדּוֹ הַחֹזֶה לְהִתְיַחֵשׂ
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The acts of Rehoboam, in genealogical form

title_english: Story (Midrash) of the Prophet Iddo
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Abijah's acts, ways and sayings
note: Possibly the same work as the other Iddo writings.

title_english: Book of Jehu son of Hanani
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last
note: The verse says it was included in the book of the kings of Israel.

title_english: Isaiah's account of the acts of Uzziah
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The acts of Uzziah, first and last, written by Isaiah son of Amoz
note: No title is given; the verse only says Isaiah wrote them. The canonical book of Isaiah contains no such account.

title_english: Vision of Isaiah son of Amoz
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Hezekiah's acts and his goodness
note: Often identified with the canonical book of Isaiah, which opens with the same Hebrew phrase (Isa 1:1, verified on Sefaria) and narrates Hezekiah's reign in chapters 36-39.

title_english: Sayings of the Seers (or of Hozai)
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Manasseh's prayer, his sin, and the high places he built
surviving_status: extant work with the same name but probably different
note: The Hebrew can be read as 'the seers' or as a proper name 'Hozai'. The apocryphal 'Prayer of Manasseh' is generally regarded by scholars as a separate, later composition, not this source.

title_english: The Lamentations (for Josiah)
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Jeremiah's laments for Josiah sung by singing men and women
note: Some traditions link it to the canonical book of Lamentations, but that book laments the fall of Jerusalem, not Josiah.

title_english: Chronicles of King David
what_the_text_says_it_contains: An official record into which Joab's unfinished census was not entered
note: A royal record, not a literary book.

title_english: Samuel's book of the manner of the kingdom
what_the_text_says_it_contains: The rules of the monarchy, written by Samuel and laid up before the LORD
note: Unnamed document; compare Deuteronomy 17:14-20.

title_english: Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia
title_hebrew_or_greek: סֵפֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים לְמַלְכֵי מָדַי וּפָרָס
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Persian court records: Mordecai's report of the plot, and the acts of Ahasuerus and Mordecai
note: Royal archive, not a religious book.

title_english: Book of the Chronicles (Levite records)
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Lists of Levite heads of fathers' houses up to Johanan son of Eliashib
note: Possibly a temple register; not necessarily the canonical Chronicles.

title_english: Epistle from Laodicea
what_the_text_says_it_contains: A letter to be read by the Colossians after it reached them from Laodicea
surviving_status: extant work with the same name but probably different
note: A short Latin 'Epistle to the Laodiceans', first attested in Codex Fuldensis and copied in medieval Latin Bibles, is a compilation of verses from other Pauline letters and is not considered the original. Some scholars suggest Colossians 4:16 refers to canonical Ephesians (per Wikipedia, checked Oct 2026).

title_english: Paul's earlier letter to the Corinthians
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Instruction not to associate with sexually immoral people
note: Some scholars have proposed that part of it may survive in 2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1; this is debated.

title_english: Prophecy of Enoch (quoted in Jude)
what_the_text_says_it_contains: Enoch's prophecy that the Lord comes with myriads of his holy ones to execute judgment on the ungodly
note: Commonly identified with 1 Enoch 1:9. The full Book of Enoch survives only in Ge'ez (Ethiopic); Aramaic fragments of its earlier sections were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls at Qumran (per Wikipedia, checked Oct 2026). Jude names no book; it quotes Enoch.
